memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and attacked it. The Lord also gave that city and its king into Israel's hand. The city and everyone in it Joshua put to the sword. He left no survivors there. And he did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho. — Josh 10:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As the campaign continues to Libnah, one small phrase deserves our attention: "The Lord also gave that city and its king into Israel's hand." This phrase, or one like it, keeps recurring throughout the chapter. City after city, the text is careful to say that it was the Lord who gave the victory. Israel fought, but God delivered. The credit is placed, again and again, squarely with Him.

This repetition is not accidental. The writer wants us to understand, beyond any doubt, that these victories were God's doing. It would have been easy, as the conquest rolled on, for Israel to begin trusting in their own momentum, their growing reputation, their battle-hardened experience. But the constant refrain, "the Lord gave," kept pointing them back to the true source of every success.

We need this same reminder. When things are going well, when we experience a string of "victories," we are tempted to start relying on ourselves — our skill, our track record, our momentum. Success can quietly erode our dependence on God. The steady refrain of this chapter calls us back: it is the Lord who gives.

Whatever good comes from our lives comes ultimately from God's hand. Jesus said, "apart from me you can do nothing" (John 15:5), and James reminds us that "every good and perfect gift is from above" (Jas 1:17). In seasons of success as much as seasons of struggle, we do well to keep saying, with this chapter, "The Lord gave." That habit of giving God the credit guards our hearts against pride and keeps us humbly dependent on Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. In seasons of success, do you keep giving God the credit, or start trusting yourself?
2. How can you cultivate the habit of saying, "The Lord gave"?
3. Where do you need to return dependence to God rather than relying on your own momentum?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, in every victory, remind me that You are the one who gives. Guard me from pride in my successes, and keep me humbly dependent on You. Amen.
